name: Barbershop
tagline: Three to five chairs, licensed barbers, and regulars who follow the person holding the clippers.

unit.name: haircut
unit.note: Price: Square lists NYC men's cuts at $77 on average, range $33-$170 (salons included); SQUIRE's shop data puts the Northeast mean near $40. A neighborhood shop sits between them: $50 before tax and tip. Cost per cut: two towels laundered $0.70, blade $0.20, neck strip $0.05, disinfectant and spray $0.15, aftershave, powder and styling product $0.40, cape cleaning $0.10 = $1.60.

market.note: Potential haircuts a month for one shop at $50 and average quality, before the share that walks away: about 560-600 served on a street with several competitors, 140-150 per chair in a 4-chair shop. SQUIRE (May 2025-April 2026, 2,224 shops) reports 94.2 appointments per barber per month on average, including part-timers; a dense NYC block runs higher. Elasticity is below coffee: 44.63% of SQUIRE clients are returning and 71% of men say they stay with one barber.

capacity.note: One full-time barber: 160 chair-hours a month at about 1.4 cuts an hour (35-45 minutes per client) = 220 haircuts at full load. Only barbers and apprentices cut hair: the front desk adds no haircuts (see engine/src/niches/barbershop.ts). A chair without a barber earns nothing.

sizing.note: Floor: a 4-chair shop takes 650-800 sq ft in total; at the game's 60% usable share that is about 100 sq ft per chair with the waiting bench and aisle. Throughput: a chair is open about 66 hours a week, a barber works 37, but demand bunches on Friday and Saturday (Friday alone is 20.47% of barbering appointments, Mangomint), so one chair serves about 1.35 barber loads: 300 cuts a month. Cleaning per chair: one 64 oz Barbicide concentrate ($15.49-$26.99) plus clipper spray, about $28. Too few chairs: Saturday clients leave. Too many: rent and empty mirrors.

setup.name: Security deposit (2 months of rent)
setup.note: 2 x $6,250: 750 sq ft at $100 per sq ft a year, between REBNY's H1 2025 asking rents for Smith Street ($90) and Court Street ($115) in Brooklyn. Small NYC landlords usually ask 2-3 months. You get it back only when the lease ends.

setup.name: Basic build-out, per chair: paint, floor, lighting, sink hook-ups
setup.note: A light refresh of a second-generation space runs $17-$30 per sq ft in contractor guides; $30 x 167 sq ft of shop per chair = $5,000. A first-generation shell costs far more: Cushman & Wakefield's 2026 in-line retail benchmark is about $157 per sq ft nationally. The Health Code requires a sink with hot and cold running water, so pick a space with plumbing.

setup.name: Custom build-out upgrade, per chair: millwork, tile, new plumbing lines
setup.note: Adds about $24 per sq ft on top of the basic refresh, for a total near $54 per sq ft: still a third of the $157 national in-line retail benchmark.

setup.name: Hydraulic barber chair (Minerva Traditional)
setup.note: Minerva Beauty Traditional Barber Chair in Black, SKU 1181b: $599. Warranty: 1 year on the chair top, 2 years on base and pump. Sales tax applies to equipment purchases (TB-ST-60).

setup.name: Upgrade to a Takara Belmont Elegance chair, per chair
setup.note: Takara Belmont Elegance 225 Classic: list price $3,862.50 at W.B. Barber Supply and at a second US retailer; minus the $599 base chair = $3,264. Sale prices from $3,450 exist; the Elite version lists at $4,313 and the Legacy near $5,950. Freight is extra.

setup.name: Wall-mount barber station with mirror
setup.note: Retail listings: OmySalon wall-mount station with mirror $199.98; BarberPub dresser station with mirror $251.91. Mid-range wall stations run $150-$300.

setup.name: Disinfection jar and Barbicide concentrate, per chair
setup.note: Barbicide disinfecting jar $39.99 plus one 64 oz concentrate $26.99 (Walmart listings; barber suppliers sell the concentrate from $15.49). Tools must be clean and sanitary for every client.

setup.name: Shop clipper set, per chair (Wahl 5 Star Senior and Andis Master)
setup.note: Wahl 5 Star Senior corded $125.50 (Pivot Point) plus Andis Improved Master corded $119.99 (barber supplier listing) = $245.49. Most barbers bring their own tools; a shop set covers apprentices and breakdowns.

setup.name: Shampoo backwash unit
setup.note: Buy-Rite Beauty Nova Shampoo Backwash Unit: $995 (list $1,045). Budget units start near $550. Needs a plumber to connect.

setup.name: Hot towel cabinet
setup.note: Puroeis medium hot towel cabinet: $210 at Pure Spa Direct. Small consumer units start near $80; 128-towel cabinets run $456 and up.

setup.name: Waiting area seating (4 seats)
setup.note: Minerva Beauty Loki Waiting Chair, set of two: list price $329 (seen on sale at $279.65). Two sets = 4 seats = $658.

setup.name: Reception desk
setup.note: Buy-Rite Beauty Square Reception Desk: $599 (list $1,295). Larger desks on the same site run $1,495-$2,995.

setup.name: Card terminal (Square Terminal)
setup.note: Square Terminal $299; Square Stand $149; Square Register (2nd generation) $899 on squareup.com/shop. The Free software plan is $0 a month.

setup.name: Storefront sign, installed by a licensed sign hanger with DOB permit
setup.note: Estimate for a small non-illuminated sign: fabrication, filing and a Licensed Sign Hanger. NYC DOB requires a permit unless the sign is painted on the building or is under 6 sq ft and not illuminated; an illuminated sign needs a separate permit renewed every year. I did not find the DOB fee schedule.

setup.name: Opening supplies: towels, capes, blades, neck strips, disinfectant, aftershave
setup.note: 15 dozen towels $300, 12 capes $180, blades and neck strips for 3 months $250, disinfectant and sprays $150, combs, brushes, guards and clips $250, aftershave, powder and styling product $250, cleaning kit $120 = $1,500.

setup.name: First retail stock: pomade, shampoo, beard oil
setup.note: About 80 units at $10 wholesale. Buy for resale with a resale certificate: you pay no sales tax on the stock and charge the customer 8.875%.

setup.name: First insurance payments: business owner's policy and workers' compensation
setup.note: Insureon medians for barbershops: business owner's policy $68 a month ($817 a year), workers' compensation $70 a month ($839 a year). National medians: a New York quote can be higher. New York requires workers' compensation as soon as you have an employee.

setup.name: Barber Shop Owner license (New York State)
setup.agency: NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
setup.note: $60 initial application, $60 renewal; NY Business Express lists a 4-year term. Needed to own, control or operate a barber shop; it does not let the owner cut hair. The wait is my estimate: the Department publishes no processing time for this license, and the state said in February 2026 that licensing now takes days instead of months.

setup.name: Barber Shop Permit (New York City)
setup.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
setup.note: NYC Health Code Art. 163. New application $7.50-$15, renewal $15 a year; every permit expires on October 31. The permit document arrives by mail in about 7-10 days. It does not replace the state license or the Certificate of Occupancy (NYC Charter §645).

kits.name: Lean start
kits.pitch: Three chairs in a space that already has plumbing. Nothing you do not need to open legally, and the most cash left for slow first months.

kits.name: Standard
kits.pitch: Four chairs, a shampoo unit, hot towels and a small retail shelf. Enough chairs for Saturday without paying rent for empty mirrors.

kits.name: Premium
kits.pitch: Five Takara Belmont chairs and a custom interior that supports a higher price. It leaves about two months of rent in the bank: one slow season can end it.

monthlyCosts.name: Electricity, gas and water
monthlyCosts.note: About 1,300 kWh a month (lighting, clippers, dryers, air conditioning, water heater) at roughly $0.26 per kWh all-in for a small Con Edison commercial account = $340, plus water and sewer $60 and gas $50. I could not open the NYSERDA and EIA tables for the exact commercial rate.

monthlyCosts.name: Business internet
monthlyCosts.note: Verizon Fios Business Internet 300 Mbps: $69 a month before taxes, fees and equipment (first-year credits can lower it). Reviews quote a business phone line at about $20 more and Spectrum Business from $65; most shops take calls on a mobile phone and the booking app.

monthlyCosts.name: Business owner's policy (general liability and property)
monthlyCosts.note: Insureon median for barbershops: $68 a month ($817 a year) with $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate limits. General liability alone: $37-$38 a month. Workers' compensation is a payroll cost and sits in the common pack.

monthlyCosts.name: Professional liability insurance
monthlyCosts.note: MoneyGeek reports $33 a month ($391 a year) for barbers; Insuranceopedia reports $54. Secondary sources, lower figure taken.

monthlyCosts.name: Private trash carter
monthlyCosts.note: NYC businesses must hire a licensed private carter. The city's maximum rate is $26.87 per cubic yard or $17.64 per 100 pounds (BIC rule adopted July 2024, Customer Bill of Rights). The volume is my estimate: about 3.5 cubic yards a month of hair, paper and packaging = $94. Carters may charge less.

monthlyCosts.name: Card processing (Square)
monthlyCosts.note: Square Free plan, $0 a month: 2.6% + 15 cents for every tap, dip or swipe (rate set on February 25, 2025). On a $50 haircut that is $1.45 = 2.9%. Assumes nearly every client pays by card or phone; card tips add fees the shop also pays.

monthlyCosts.name: Bookkeeper
monthlyCosts.note: Monthly bookkeeping and quarterly sales tax returns for a small shop, about $250. Not checked against a published price list: ask two local bookkeepers for a quote.

monthlyCosts.name: Payroll service, base fee (Gusto Simple)
monthlyCosts.note: Gusto Simple plan: $49 a month (raised from $40 on March 1, 2026) plus $6 per person. Files payroll taxes and W-2s.

monthlyCosts.name: Payroll service, per worker
monthlyCosts.note: Gusto Simple plan: $6 per person per month on top of the $49 base.

monthlyCosts.name: Basic marketing: online listing, photos, local ads
monthlyCosts.note: A free Google Business Profile and Instagram page plus about $200 a month of local ads and printed cards. Owner's choice, not a quoted price.

monthlyCosts.name: Blade sharpening and chair repairs, per chair
monthlyCosts.note: Clipper blade sharpening or replacement about $12 a month per station plus a reserve for hydraulic pumps and upholstery, $8.

monthlyCosts.name: Clipper oil, guards, spray and small tools, per worker
monthlyCosts.note: Clipper oil and coolant spray, replacement guards and combs, about $25 per barber a month. Per-cut consumables are in the cost per haircut.

monthlyCosts.name: Licensed background music
monthlyCosts.note: Third-party guides quote Soundtrack Your Brand at about $35-$36 a month per location in the US; the vendor's own price page was not seen. A personal streaming account is not licensed for a shop.

monthlyCosts.name: License and permit renewals, set aside monthly
monthlyCosts.note: State shop license renewal $60 every 4 years = $1.25 a month; city Barber Shop Permit $15 every year = $1.25 a month.

staff.name: Licensed barber
staff.licenseRequired: NYS Barber Operator license (Department of State): $40, renewal $40, practical exam $15
staff.note: BLS OEWS May 2023, barbers (39-5011), New York-Newark-Jersey City: mean $22.30 an hour, $46,390 a year, 2,090 employed. I found no later BLS metro figure. New York allows no tip credit in miscellaneous industries since December 31, 2020, so the cash wage equals the full wage; tips come on top and belong to the barber.

staff.name: Barber apprentice
staff.licenseRequired: NYS Barber Apprentice certificate ($20); must work under a licensed barber
staff.note: NYC minimum wage from January 1, 2026: $17.00 an hour, with no tip credit. An apprentice must be 17 or older and pass a medical exam; two years of licensed apprenticeship (or a state-approved barber school) lead to the exam. An apprentice may not own a shop or rent a chair. In the game an apprentice produces 60% of a barber's haircuts.

staff.name: Front desk
staff.note: BLS OEWS May 2023, receptionists and information clerks (43-4171), New York-Newark-Jersey City: mean $20.27 an hour. Books clients, takes payment, sweeps. Cuts no hair.

taxes.name: NYC sales tax on barbering services
taxes.appliesIf: haircuts, shaves and other barbering services sold in New York City
taxes.note: Barbering services carry only the 4.5% New York City tax: no state tax and no MCTD surcharge. Outside the city the service is not taxed at all (Tax Bulletin TB-ST-60). Charged on top of the price and held for the state.

taxes.name: Sales tax on retail products
taxes.appliesIf: retail products only: pomade, shampoo, beard oil sold to take home
taxes.note: Products sold to customers are taxed at the full combined rate in New York City: 8.875%. This rate applies to retail revenue only, never to haircuts: see extra.salesTax.

options.label: Cleaning service twice a week plus nightly mop
Staff sweep after every cut and mop every night
Sweep when it piles up, mop once a week
Booking app plus paid marketplace promotion
Sell pomade, shampoo and beard oil
Hot towel finish and a drink for every client

shortcuts.name: Call your barbers 1099 contractors
shortcuts.what: No payroll taxes, no workers' comp. But you set their hours and prices, so the state sees employees. A real chair renter needs a state Area Renter license.

shortcuts.name: Put an unlicensed barber on a chair
shortcuts.what: One chair worked at minimum wage instead of a licensed barber's pay. If a state investigator walks in, the owner answers, not only the barber.

shortcuts.name: Skip disinfecting tools between clients
shortcuts.what: Saves disinfectant and a few minutes a cut. Dirty clippers spread ringworm and folliculitis, and one photo in a review is enough.

shortcuts.name: Let the shop license and city permit lapse
shortcuts.what: Skips the $60 state renewal and the $15 city renewal. You save $2.50 a month and run an unlicensed shop.

shortcuts.name: Sell retail products without sales tax
shortcuts.what: Pomade for cash, no 8.875% charged or sent to the state. The tax is still owed, by you personally, with penalties.

shortcuts.name: Closing and Saturday hours off the clock
shortcuts.what: The timesheet stops at 40 hours; cleaning, closing and the Saturday rush go unpaid. New York requires time and a half past 40 hours, and a barber can claim six years back.

shortcuts.name: Pay commission only, no minimum-wage floor
shortcuts.what: In a slow week a barber's share falls below $17 an hour and you pay just the share. The law requires the minimum for every hour worked.

shortcuts.name: Keep a cut of card tips
shortcuts.what: Hold back a 'processing fee' from tips paid by card. Tips belong to the barber: the employer may not keep any part.

shortcuts.name: Put shop trash out with the residential pickup
shortcuts.what: Cancel the private carter and leave bags at the curb for the city truck. Businesses must use a licensed carter.

shortcuts.name: Leave cash haircuts out of the register
shortcuts.what: Cash cuts never reach the books: no sales tax, no income tax on them. Auditors compare your chairs, hours and supplies with what you report.

violations.name: Operating a barber shop without a state license
violations.law: NY General Business Law Art. 28: §432 (license required), §441(a) (fine up to $500), §444 (misdemeanor)
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor under GBL §444: up to 6 months in jail, a fine up to $500, or both. Each violation is a separate offense.
violations.note: The statute caps the fine at $500 per violation and counts each violation separately. The game charges $500 when found plus $500 for each month open, up to $3,000: the monthly step and the cap are game rules.

violations.name: Operating without the city Barber Shop Permit
violations.law: NYC Health Code §163.03 (permit required), §3.11(b) (operating without a valid permit)
violations.note: City penalty schedule: Health Code §3.11(b), operating without a currently valid permit, standard penalty $1,000, default penalty $2,000 (if you do not answer the summons). OATH's guide for barbershops gives the range $200-$2,000 for §163.03.

violations.name: Unlicensed barber working in the shop
violations.law: NY General Business Law Art. 28: §441(a), §444 (owner who permits an unlicensed person to practice)
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor under GBL §444 for the barber and for the owner who allows it: up to 6 months, a fine up to $500, or both, per violation. A revoked shop license cannot be reissued for one year.
violations.note: $500 is the statutory cap per violation and each violation is a separate offense. Game rule: $500 when found plus two violations for each month it lasted (the unlicensed work and the owner who permitted it). The Department can also suspend or revoke the shop license (§441).

violations.name: Operating on an expired license or permit
violations.law: NY General Business Law §439 (renewal), §441(a), §444; NYC Health Code §3.11(b)
violations.note: An expired license is no license: fine up to $500 per violation (GBL §441(a)). Renewing within a year of expiry costs $10 extra (§439); after 5 years a barber must retake the exam. The city permit expires every October 31; operating without a valid one is $1,000 on the city schedule. Monthly step and cap are game rules.

violations.name: Tools not cleaned and disinfected between clients
violations.law: NYC Health Code §163.05 (implements must be clean and sanitary); 10 NYCRR §10.24; NY General Business Law §441(a)
violations.note: GBL §441(a): a fine up to $500, suspension or revocation for violating the article, its rules or any applicable sanitary code. The city Health Code adds its own penalties ($200-$2,000 range in OATH's barbershop guide). Monthly step and cap are game rules.

violations.name: Unsanitary shop: floor, towels, waste
violations.law: NYC Health Code §163.05 (covered receptacles, clean towels), §163.11 (floor swept and mopped at least daily); 10 NYCRR §10.20
violations.note: The rule is real: the floor must be swept and mopped at least once a day, hair removed as soon as practicable. I did not find Article 163 in the city's fixed penalty schedule, so the amount uses the $200-$2,000 range from OATH's barbershop guide: $200 plus $100 per month of neglect.

violations.name: Employees treated as independent contractors
violations.law: NY Labor Law Art. 18 (unemployment insurance contributions); NY Workers' Compensation Law §52; NY General Business Law Art. 28 (Area Renter license)
violations.criminal: Failing to carry workers' compensation is a crime under WCL §52: fines from $1,000 to $50,000 on conviction. An injured uninsured worker can also sue the owner.
violations.note: Workers' Compensation Board: misrepresenting employees as independent contractors can bring a fine up to $2,000 for every 10 days without coverage, or twice the cost of compensation. The game charges the unpaid payroll taxes back with 25% on top, plus $2,000 a month: a third of the WCL maximum. Back unemployment contributions and interest are owed as well.

violations.name: Unpaid overtime
violations.law: NY Labor Law §198, §663; 12 NYCRR Part 142 (overtime at 1.5 times the regular rate after 40 hours)
violations.criminal: Repeated or willful failure to pay wages is a misdemeanor, and a felony for a repeat offender, under NY Labor Law §198-a.
violations.note: The employer owes the unpaid wages plus liquidated damages of 100%, so twice what was saved, plus interest; claims reach back six years. For a willful or repeat violation the Department can add a civil penalty up to double the wages due (Labor Law §218).

violations.name: Pay below the minimum wage
violations.law: NY Labor Law §652 (minimum wage), §663; 12 NYCRR Part 142
violations.note: NYC minimum wage is $17.00 an hour in 2026 and there is no tip credit for barbers. Commission is legal only if it never falls below the minimum for the hours worked. Back wages plus 100% liquidated damages (Labor Law §663), six years back.

violations.name: Employer keeping part of the tips
violations.note: No employer or agent may demand, accept or keep any part of an employee's gratuities. The barber recovers the tips plus 100% liquidated damages.

violations.name: Sales tax not collected or not paid
violations.law: NY Tax Law §1105, §1133 (personal liability), §1145 (penalties); NYC Administrative Code §11-2002(h)
violations.criminal: Willful failure to collect or pay over sales tax can be prosecuted as tax fraud under NY Tax Law Art. 37.
violations.note: You owe the tax itself plus a penalty of 10% for the first month and 1% for each month after, up to 30%, never less than $50, plus interest. Omitting more than 25% of the tax on a return adds 10%. The owner is personally liable: the state can take personal assets.

violations.name: Commercial waste without a licensed carter
violations.law: NYC Administrative Code §16-116 (commercial waste removal); DSNY rules for businesses
violations.note: DSNY: every business must use a private carter or register as a self-hauler; the fine for this rule is $50-$100, and improper set-out is $50, $100, then $200 for repeat offenses. The $600 cap is a game rule.

violations.name: Cash sales kept off the books
violations.law: NY Tax Law §1145 (sales tax penalties) and Art. 37 (tax fraud); 26 U.S.C. §6663 (civil fraud penalty)
violations.criminal: Hiding sales to evade tax is tax fraud: a crime under NY Tax Law Art. 37 and 26 U.S.C. §7201.
violations.note: Placeholder until the common pack arrives: the tax saved is owed back, plus the federal civil fraud penalty of 75% of the underpayment. Agent 14 owns the exact rule; this id is listed for him in agents/15.md.

officials.name: State license investigator
officials.agency: NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
officials.realProcess: Anyone can file a written complaint about unlicensed work; the Department does not show it to the shop. A license investigator visits unannounced and asks for the shop license and each barber's license. Violations go to an administrative hearing: a fine up to $500, suspension or revocation.

officials.name: City health inspector
officials.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
officials.realProcess: The inspector checks the permit, the sink with hot and cold water, towels, covered bins, tools and the floor. A summons is answered at a hearing at the city's Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings; ignoring it doubles the penalty.

officials.name: Sanitation enforcement agent
officials.realProcess: Agents check bags left at the curb for commercial waste and look for the carter's decal in the window. First offense $50, then $100, then $200.

officials.name: Labor standards investigator
officials.realProcess: One worker's claim opens the payroll of the whole shop. The investigator asks for time records, pay stubs and tip records for up to six years; missing records are read against the employer.

officials.name: State tax auditor
officials.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
officials.realProcess: A sales tax audit compares returns with bank deposits, card reports and purchases. If records are poor, the auditor estimates sales from chairs, hours and supplies and bills the difference with penalty and interest.

reports.name: Report an unlicensed shop or barber (NYS Department of State)
reports.text: A state license investigator visits unannounced and checks every license on the wall. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report unsanitary conditions (311)
reports.text: The Health Department checks the permit, tools, towels and floor. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report business trash at the curb (311)
reports.text: A sanitation agent checks whose bags they are and whether the shop has a licensed carter. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report wage theft or fake contractors (NYS Department of Labor)
reports.text: A labor investigator audits pay, hours, tips and who is really an employee. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report sales tax evasion (NYS Tax Department)
reports.text: A state auditor compares the shop's returns with its real sales. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

events.name: Back-to-school rush
events.text: Every kid in the neighborhood needs a cut before the first day of school.
events.note: SQUIRE describes late August and early September as a seasonal peak; the size of the lift is my estimate.

events.name: Holiday rush
events.text: Office parties and family photos fill the chairs in December.
events.note: December is the busiest month in shop booking data; +15% is an estimate inside the game's event limits.

events.name: January slump
events.text: After the holidays clients stretch the time between cuts.
events.note: The average gap between visits is 48.5 days (SQUIRE); after a December peak, January bookings dip. The size is an estimate.

events.name: Prom and wedding season
events.text: Proms, graduations and weddings bring fades and hot-towel shaves in May and June.
events.note: Seasonal pattern known to shop owners; the size is an estimate.

events.name: Con Edison rate increase
events.text: The state approved higher electric and gas delivery rates. Your utility bill goes up.
events.note: The Public Service Commission adopted a three-year Con Edison rate plan on January 22, 2026: $234 million more electric revenue in the first year. Press reports put the 2026 bill increase at about 3.5-3.6%; the state summary's own percentage was not seen, so +4% is an estimate.

events.name: Flu season
events.text: Two barbers call in sick in the same week. Fewer hands on the chairs.
events.note: Flu activity in the US peaks between December and February (CDC). NYC paid safe and sick leave gives workers at shops with 5-99 employees up to 40 paid hours a year. The 8% is an estimate.

events.name: Weekend subway work
events.text: No trains at your station on weekends this month. Saturday walk-ins drop.
events.note: The MTA posts planned weekend service changes; the effect on foot traffic is an estimate.

ruleCards.title: Two licenses before the first cut
ruleCards.text: A barber shop in NYC needs the state Barber Shop Owner license ($60, NYS Department of State) and the city Barber Shop Permit ($15 a year, expires every Oct 31). Opening without them: up to $500 per violation from the state, $1,000 from the city.

ruleCards.title: The shop license does not let you cut
ruleCards.text: The Barber Shop Owner license lets you own and run the shop. It does not permit you to practice barbering: every person who cuts hair needs their own state barber license.

ruleCards.title: Every barber needs a state license
ruleCards.text: A NY barber license costs $40 plus a $15 exam. It takes two years as a licensed apprentice or a course at a state-approved barber school. Letting an unlicensed person cut is a misdemeanor for the owner too: up to $500 or 6 months per violation.

ruleCards.title: Apprentices
ruleCards.text: A barber apprentice needs a state certificate ($20), must be at least 17, pass a medical exam and work under a licensed barber. An apprentice may not own a shop or rent a chair. Pay is at least the $17.00 NYC minimum wage.

ruleCards.title: Chair rental has its own license
ruleCards.text: A barber who works in your shop but is not your employee is an independent contractor and needs a state Area Renter license ($60) on top of the barber license. Chair rent is rent of real property: no sales tax on it.

ruleCards.title: Renter or employee?
ruleCards.text: If you set a barber's hours, prices and clients, the state treats them as your employee whatever the contract says. Workers' comp fines for fake contractors run up to $2,000 for every 10 days without coverage, plus the unpaid payroll taxes.

ruleCards.title: No tip credit for barbers
ruleCards.text: Since Dec 31, 2020 New York allows no tip credit outside hospitality. A barber must get the full minimum wage, $17.00 an hour in NYC in 2026, before tips. Tips belong to the barber: the shop may not keep any part.

ruleCards.title: Overtime and wage claims
ruleCards.text: Over 40 hours a week is paid at 1.5 times the regular rate. Unpaid wages are owed back with 100% liquidated damages, so twice the amount, and a worker can claim six years back.

ruleCards.title: Haircuts are taxed only in the city
ruleCards.text: Barbering services are exempt from sales tax in New York State, except in New York City, where a 4.5% city tax applies. Charge it on top of the price and send it to the state.

ruleCards.title: Products are taxed at 8.875%
ruleCards.text: Pomade, shampoo and beard oil sold to take home are taxed at the full 8.875% in NYC. Chairs, mirrors and clippers you buy for the shop are taxable too. Products used up during a cut are not resold: you pay tax when you buy them.

ruleCards.title: Sales tax is not your money
ruleCards.text: Late or unpaid sales tax costs 10% for the first month plus 1% for each month after, up to 30%, never less than $50, plus interest. The owner is personally liable: the state can take personal assets, LLC or not.

ruleCards.title: Clean and sanitary, every client
ruleCards.text: No tool may be used on a client unless it is clean and sanitary. The shop needs a sink with hot and cold running water, fresh or single-use towels, and covered bins for used linen and for hair. State fine: up to $500 per violation.

ruleCards.title: Mop every day
ruleCards.text: The NYC Health Code requires the floor of a barber shop to be swept and mopped at least once a day, and hair removed as soon as practicable. The licensed owner is responsible for keeping the shop sanitary at all times.

ruleCards.title: Businesses pay for their own trash
ruleCards.text: The city does not collect business waste. Every NYC business must hire a licensed private carter or register as a self-hauler. The city caps the rate at $26.87 per cubic yard. Fines for skipping it start at $50-$100.

ruleCards.title: Signs need a permit
ruleCards.text: A business sign needs a NYC Buildings permit unless it is painted on the building or is under 6 square feet and not illuminated. Hanging it takes a Licensed Sign Hanger. An illuminated sign needs its own permit, renewed every year.

ruleCards.title: Check the Certificate of Occupancy
ruleCards.text: The city permit does not let you use the space. Under NYC Charter §645 you need a Certificate of Occupancy from the Buildings Department before you can use your shop. Check what the building's certificate allows before you sign the lease.

ruleCards.title: Clients follow the barber
ruleCards.text: 71% of men say they are loyal to one barber or stylist, and 44.63% of barbershop clients are returning clients. When a barber leaves, a share of the shop's regulars leaves with them. Pay and respect are retention tools.

roadmap.title: Decide how your barbers will work
roadmap.text: Employees on hourly pay or commission, or true chair renters who run their own book. It decides your payroll taxes, your control and which licenses each person needs. Typical commission is 50-60% to the barber; NYC chair rent runs $230-$460 a week.

roadmap.title: Learn who may hold the clippers
roadmap.text: The owner's license lets you run the shop, not cut hair. Only state-licensed barbers and registered apprentices may cut. If you plan to cut yourself, you need your own barber license: two years of apprenticeship or barber school, then a $15 exam and a $40 license.

roadmap.title: Find a storefront that can legally be a barber shop
roadmap.text: Look for 150-200 sq ft per chair, existing plumbing for sinks, and a Certificate of Occupancy that allows the use. A former salon or barber shop saves tens of thousands in build-out. Compare rent with expected sales: above 15% of revenue is dangerous.

roadmap.title: Sign the lease and pay the deposit
roadmap.text: Expect a security deposit of two to three months of rent and a personal guarantee. Ask for free rent during build-out and permit waiting: rent runs from day one whether you are open or not. Have a lawyer read the lease.

roadmap.title: Buy insurance before anyone works
roadmap.text: Workers' compensation and disability coverage are required as soon as you have one employee. Add a business owner's policy for liability and property: about $68 a month for a barbershop. Landlords usually demand a liability certificate.

roadmap.title: Apply for the state Barber Shop Owner license
roadmap.text: Apply online in the NYS License Center once you have the business name and address. $60. You must be at least 18. Display the license in the shop. Do not cut a single head before it is issued.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services

roadmap.title: Apply for the city Barber Shop Permit
roadmap.text: Apply to the NYC Health Department with the required documents checklist. $15 or less for the first year; it expires every October 31. The permit arrives by mail in about 7-10 days.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

roadmap.title: Build out the shop to the Health Code
roadmap.text: You need a sink with hot and cold running water, a soap dispenser, covered bins for used towels and for hair, and a floor you can mop daily. Plumbing and electrical work needs licensed trades and may need Buildings Department permits.

roadmap.title: Order chairs, stations and disinfection gear
roadmap.text: One hydraulic chair, one mirror station and one disinfectant jar per barber. New mid-range chairs start near $600; a Takara Belmont runs $3,900 and up. Order early: freight takes weeks. You pay sales tax on equipment.

roadmap.title: Register to collect sales tax
roadmap.text: Get a Certificate of Authority from the NYS Tax Department before your first sale. In NYC you charge 4.5% on haircuts and 8.875% on products, and file returns every quarter. The money is held in trust for the state.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance

roadmap.title: Get the sign permit and hang the sign
roadmap.text: Signs over 6 sq ft or illuminated need a Buildings Department permit, and a Licensed Sign Hanger must install them. Check the zoning rules for your street before you pay for fabrication.

roadmap.title: Sign up a private trash carter
roadmap.text: Businesses may not use city trash pickup. Hire a licensed carter, post the decal in your window and keep the contract. The city caps the price at $26.87 per cubic yard.

roadmap.title: Set up booking and the card terminal
roadmap.text: Pick one system for appointments, payments and client records. A card terminal costs about $299; processing is about 2.6% + 15 cents a payment; a booking app runs about $30 a month plus $20 per extra barber.

roadmap.title: Hire licensed barbers
roadmap.text: Check every license in the state's public license search before the first shift and keep copies. Put pay terms in writing. A renter needs an Area Renter license and your signed affirmation; an employee goes on payroll from day one.

roadmap.title: Stock supplies and post what the law requires
roadmap.text: Towels, capes, blades, neck strips and disinfectant for the first months. Display the shop license, the city permit and each barber's license where clients can see them, and post the labor law notices for staff.

roadmap.title: Open the doors
roadmap.text: Open only when both the state license and the city permit are on the wall. Start with a soft opening week: friends, neighbors, and photos of real cuts for your booking page. Regulars build slowly, about one visit every seven weeks each.

suppliers.what: Hydraulic chairs, mirror stations, shampoo units, waiting seating, reception desks.
suppliers.whereToFind: Salon equipment dealers with showrooms in the NY-NJ area and online catalogs; used chairs from closing shops on Craigslist and Facebook Marketplace; ask other shop owners who installed their chairs.
suppliers.examples: Minerva Beauty, Buy-Rite Beauty, Keller International, W.B. Barber Supply (Takara Belmont)
suppliers.note: Minerva, Buy-Rite and W.B. Barber Supply prices are quoted in setup; Keller International named from memory, not checked.

suppliers.what: Clippers, trimmers, shavers, shears, guards, blades and blade sharpening.
suppliers.whereToFind: Barber supply stores and their websites; brand sites for warranty registration. Barbers usually own their tools, but the shop keeps a spare set.
suppliers.examples: Wahl Professional, Andis, BaBylissPRO; W.B. Barber Supply, Barber Depots
suppliers.note: W.B. Barber Supply and Barber Depots appear in search results as online barber suppliers.

suppliers.what: Barbicide, neck strips, razor blades, capes, gloves, aftershave, talc, cleaning supplies.
suppliers.whereToFind: Professional beauty distributors that sell to license holders, barber supply stores, and wholesale clubs for paper goods and cleaning products.
suppliers.examples: SalonCentric, CosmoProf, Marlo Beauty Supply, Sally Beauty
suppliers.note: Marlo Beauty Supply states it sells only to licensed professionals and students; license rules of the other distributors were not checked.

suppliers.what: Pomade, clay, shampoo, beard oil bought wholesale and sold at about double the cost.
suppliers.whereToFind: Open a wholesale account directly with a brand or through a wholesale marketplace; give the seller a resale certificate so you do not pay sales tax on stock.
suppliers.examples: Reuzel, Layrite, Suavecito, Blind Barber (on Faire)
suppliers.note: Blind Barber's Faire listing appears in search results; the other brands are named from memory.

suppliers.what: Fresh towels for every client: a linen service that delivers and picks up, or your own washer and dryer.
suppliers.whereToFind: Commercial linen and uniform services that cover your borough, or a nearby laundromat with wash-and-fold accounts for businesses. Compare the per-towel price with your cut count.
suppliers.note: Named from memory; prices were not found.

suppliers.what: Online booking, reminders, card payments, tips, client records and reports in one system.
suppliers.whereToFind: Compare the barbershop plans on each vendor's site: monthly fee per barber, processing rate, marketplace fees for new clients, and who owns the client list if you leave.
suppliers.examples: Square Appointments, Booksy, SQUIRE, Vagaro, Mangomint
suppliers.note: Square Free: $0 a month, 2.6% + 15 cents in person (squareup.com pricing). Booksy: $29.99 a month plus $20 for each additional team member, plus tax (biz.booksy.com/pricing); card reader 2.49% + 10 cents.

suppliers.what: Business owner's policy, professional liability, workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave coverage.
suppliers.whereToFind: An independent broker who insures salons, or an online marketplace for small business quotes. For workers' compensation, the New York State Insurance Fund writes any employer.
suppliers.examples: Insureon, NEXT Insurance, Hiscox, New York State Insurance Fund (NYSIF)
suppliers.note: Insureon medians are quoted in monthlyCosts; the other insurers are named from memory.

suppliers.what: A licensed carter for the shop's waste and recycling.
suppliers.whereToFind: The city publishes the list of licensed carters and the maximum rates; in a Commercial Waste Zone you choose among the carters awarded to your zone.
suppliers.examples: Waste Connections, Interstate Waste Services, Action Carting
suppliers.note: Carter names appear in search results on Commercial Waste Zones; zone assignments were not checked.

suppliers.whereToFind: State-approved barber schools place graduates; barbers show their work on Instagram; job boards list chairs and commission offers. Verify every license in the state's public search.
suppliers.note: American Barber Institute named from memory, not checked.

manager.note: BLS OEWS May 2023, first-line supervisors of personal service workers (39-1022), New York-Newark-Jersey City: mean $28.72 an hour, $59,740 a year, 9,200 employed. $59,740 / 12 = $4,978 a month, before employer payroll taxes.

benchmarks.note: Planning ranges from trade and vendor guides, not audited data: supplies 3-10% of revenue, labor 40-50%, rent 10-15% (above 18% is a warning sign), net margin 10-15% for an independent shop. Midpoints taken. BizBuySell's dataset is paywalled.

extra.howNumbersWereChecked: The session had no direct access to source sites (network policy), only web search. 'verified' means the number appeared in a search excerpt of the primary source page itself; 'estimate' means a secondary source or my own calculation, shown in the note. Full pages were not opened: see research/reports/15-barbershop.md.

rentByTier.unit: USD per sq ft per year, ground-floor retail asking rent

prime.example: North 6th Street, Williamsburg: average asking rent $275 (REBNY H1 2025)

mid.example: Between Smith Street ($90) and Court Street ($115), Brooklyn (REBNY H1 2025)

cheap.example: Astoria, Queens side-street listings at $45-$60 per sq ft a year

rentByTier.note: Corridor averages from REBNY for prime and mid; the cheap tier rests on two individual Queens listings. A barbershop cannot carry a prime corridor at $50 a cut: rent alone would exceed half of sales.

weekdayDemand.order: Mon..Sun, same as GameDate.weekday 0..6; the seven numbers sum to 7
weekdayDemand.note: Mangomint: Friday 20.47% of barbering appointments, Thursday 18.18%, Wednesday 16.75%, Saturday 15.98%; Sunday and Monday are low because many shops close. Friday is set to 20% (1.4/7). Saturday is raised to the same level for a walk-in neighborhood shop, which Mangomint's appointment-only clients under-count: that part is my estimate.

staffLoyalty.note: followShare = 44.63% returning clients (SQUIRE) x 71% loyal to a single barber (Salon Today, 2015 Men's Grooming Study) = 32% of a departing barber's clients leave with them. Both inputs are published; no survey measures the follow rate itself, so the product is an upper-bound estimate. The hook applies the loss for the month in which the barber count drops.

hourly.note: Wage from staff[].hourlyWage. Overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours a week.

commission.note: The barber gets the larger of 50% of their haircut revenue or the hourly wage for all hours worked. The hook adds the top-up as a payroll line. Typical splits are 50/50 to 60/40 in the barber's favor (SQUIRE, Vagaro).

boothRental.note: NYC listings on SalonRenter (5 listings): $230-$461.89 a week, average $367.81. A true renter sets their own prices and hours, keeps their sales, holds a state Area Renter license ($60) and pays rent that is not subject to sales tax. Not playable in version 1: the shop's income would be rent, not haircuts.

payModels.payrollTaxNote: Employer cost on top of wages for a barber at $22.30 x 160 hours x 12 = $42,816 a year, 2026 rates: Social Security and Medicare 7.65% = $3,275; NY unemployment insurance for a new employer 4.1% of the first $17,600 = $721.60; federal unemployment 0.6% of the first $7,000 = $42; disability benefits about $18; workers' compensation about $210 (Insureon: $839 a year for a shop of four). Total $4,267 = 10.0% of wages. MCTMT is zero below $312,500 of payroll a quarter; paid family leave is withheld from the worker. The exact rates belong to packs/_common.json; this rate is used only for the commission top-up line, the 1099 shortcut and the report.

retail.note: With the retail lever on 'shelf': one client in ten buys a $25 product = $2.50 of retail revenue per haircut, bought wholesale at half the price. That is about 5% of shop revenue. Estimate; trade guides put retail at 5-15% of barbershop sales.

salesTax.note: Haircuts: 4.5% (New York City tax only). Retail products: 8.875%. The 8.875% general rate in packs/_common.json must not be applied to haircut revenue. Chair rent received from an Area Renter is not taxable.

apprentice.note: An apprentice works under a licensed barber and is slower: 60% of a barber's haircuts in the game. Estimate.

frontDesk.note: With a front desk the barbers do not stop to answer the phone or take payment: +5% haircuts per barber. Estimate.

licenses.versusAppearanceEnhancement: A barber shop is licensed under General Business Law Article 28; hair salons, nail salons and other appearance enhancement businesses are licensed under Article 27 with their own business license and rules (19 NYCRR Part 160). The city says a shop serving both kinds of work needs both licenses.
